Keep the assistant for the questions: Asking out loud how a customer is trending, or where the cash is, is a genuinely useful thing and VOS cannot do it. Those questions keep their home, and the order stops being one of them.

Shrink the pile that needs extracting: Each account you move across sends a structured, approved order rather than a voicemail. Whatever is doing the extracting has less to work through, and the hardest messages are the ones that leave first.
One place for it to land, whatever else you run: Whatever you add, the order still lands in the one system you chose, over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, so nobody ends up with two places to look.

@graph.name: Is VOS a real GrubMarket AI alternative, and is it better than GrubMarket AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: They use the same technology at opposite ends. GrubAssist is for your staff: ask it about the business, have it write up an order. VOS is for your customers: they speak it and approve it, so your staff never build one. For getting an order in without anyone on your side building it, we think VOS is better, because the buyer does the work and signs it off. For asking your data questions out loud, no, and not by a little: VOS does not do that at all.

@graph.name: Can VOS tell us how a customer is performing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can see what an account has ordered, and that is the extent of it. Business analysis, cash flow, anomaly spotting: all of that is on their list and none of it is on ours. Worth knowing before you shortlist us against them.

@graph.name: Do we have to teach VOS our catalog?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and there is no module for it, because nothing has to be taught. The item list you keep for an account is the configuration. Load it, and spoken items land on the right rows at the price you hold.

@graph.name: Does any of this touch our ERP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only to hand it the order. It never goes near your ERP beyond handing in what the buyer approved. GrubAssist connects to an ERP so it can answer questions about the business; VOS only ever delivers into one. Everything downstream behaves exactly as it did yesterday.

Neither of us publishes a figure. Ours arrives as a quote once we know your setup. Theirs comes after a demo. With that much on their side, the thing to pin down is which ones the quote actually covers.

@graph.name: How soon could our accounts be ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens place one the same day. There is no training phase, which is the bulk of the difference. They publish no timeline, so ask them for one rather than take a number from us.

@graph.name: And the accounts that will only ever call?

acceptedAnswer.text: They carry on telephoning, and your desk deals with those the way it always has. Be clear about the limit though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number from VOS, no timestamp and nothing moving in stock. Only what comes through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the GrubMarket details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Taken from grubmarket.ai on 10 October 2026, which is the GrubMarket AI product rather than GrubMarket the company: the GrubAssist description, the list of advertised jobs, the training module and the other products all come off that page.
